title: fix(service-settings): redact encrypted setting values at the REST read boundary (#7522)
body:
Fixes #7522

## What was exposed

`GET /api/settings/:namespace` returned the **plaintext** of every encrypted setting in the namespace:

- in `values.[key].value`, and
- repeated once more inside **every** `cascadeChain` entry (global / tenant / user / env).

Both specifier flavours were affected — `type: 'password'` and an explicit `encrypted: true`.

Storage was never the problem, and the issue's root-cause reading held up against the tree I checked out: `sys_setting.value` is null, `value_enc` holds a `sec_` handle, `sys_secret` holds the aes-256-gcm ciphertext. The leak was entirely on the way out. `materialiseRow()` (`settings-service.ts:1870`) dereferences the handle and decrypts; `get()` copies that plaintext into each chain entry (`:1068` / `:1082` / `:1094`); `getNamespace()` (`:1118`) returns it; and the `GET` handler in `settings-routes.ts` handed the payload straight to `sendOk` — no redaction anywhere on the path.

The endpoint requires `setup.access`, so this is **defense-in-depth, not privilege escalation**. It is still a real exposure: any operator or integration holding setup access — and any log, proxy, browser cache or HAR capture on that response path — received the cleartext of every secret in the namespace, which is exactly what the `value_enc` + `sys_secret` split exists to prevent.

## What is now redacted

At the REST boundary only. The mask shape is **not invented here** — it reuses the convention ADR-0100 pins for encrypted *fields* on the generic CRUD path (`SECRET_MASK` in `@objectstack/objectql`, the read-mask + no-op-echoed-mask pair the `records-forms.encrypted-field-behavior` checklist item exercises):

- **Read.** A set secret is served as `SETTINGS_SECRET_MASK` — `••••••••`, byte-identical to objectql's mask. An unset one stays `null`, so the redaction is **presence-preserving** and the console still renders "configured vs not configured". `cascadeChain` is masked entry by entry rather than dropped, so "global sets this, your user overrides it" still renders — only the values go.
- **Write.** A submitted value equal to the mask means "unchanged", so the key is **dropped from the patch** instead of being persisted as the mask's literal text. Scoped to secret keys: a plain setting whose value genuinely is eight bullets still writes verbatim.
- **`PUT`'s own response** is redacted the same way. It carries resolved values too — including cascade entries the caller never submitted (an upper-scope secret it may not have set), so it is the same boundary.

`source`, `locked`, `lockedReason` and the `409 SETTINGS_LOCKED` env-lock behaviour are untouched, and pinned by tests.

## What deliberately still returns plaintext

`SettingsService` keeps decrypting. `materialiseRow()`, `get()`, `getNamespace()`, `snapshotOf()` and `createClient()` all still hand back **real plaintext**, because the mail / sms / storage / auth plugins read their credentials through exactly that path. A test pins that round-trip so this cannot later be "fixed" one layer down — which would break every in-process consumer.

The boundary, stated plainly: **decryption is the service's job; not-emitting-it is the route's.**

## Where the encrypted-key set comes from

`SettingsService.secretKeysOf(namespace)` publishes the registry's own `encryptedKeys` set — literally the set `setMany` consults to decide what gets encrypted. The route reads that rather than re-deriving `spec.encrypted || spec.type === 'password'`, because re-deriving the predicate at the boundary is how the two sides drift into "encrypted on write, cleartext on read". It throws `UnknownNamespaceError` for an unregistered namespace rather than answering an empty set: "I don't know this namespace" must never read as "nothing here is secret".

## Verification

`pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-settings test` — **395 passed / 18 files**, 10 of them new, all at the **route** level:

```
✓ GET /:ns leaks no ciphertext-backed cleartext — both flavours, value AND cascadeChain
✓ redaction is presence-preserving: an UNSET secret stays null, not a mask
✓ `source` and `locked` survive the redaction unchanged
✓ an env-locked secret is masked while `source: env` / `locked` / 409 SETTINGS_LOCKED are unchanged
✓ PUTting the echoed mask back is a NO-OP — the stored secret is not overwritten
✓ the echoed mask inside the read-shape {values:{k:{value}}} envelope is a no-op too
✓ a REAL new secret still writes, and the write RESPONSE is redacted too
✓ a non-encrypted key whose value genuinely IS the mask is written verbatim
✓ in-process consumers still receive REAL plaintext (createClient / snapshotOf)
✓ secretKeysOf reports both flavours and refuses an unknown namespace
```

The leak case is asserted **whole-body** (`JSON.stringify(response)` contains none of the three plaintexts, one of them seeded at `global` scope so `cascadeChain` carries a second ciphertext-backed entry) *and* per-surface, so a regression names which surface broke rather than just "a string appeared". The secrets are real ciphertext — `LocalCryptoProvider` + a `sys_secret` store, `sec_` handles, the production code path.

**Reverse verification** — direction predicted before running. Took the route fix out with `git checkout origin/main -- settings-routes.ts` (never `git stash`) and re-ran: **6 of the 10 went red**, and the 4 that stayed green are exactly those whose subject the route revert does not touch — the `source`/`locked` passthrough, the non-secret verbatim write, the in-process plaintext guard, and `secretKeysOf` (which lives in the service). Restored and re-ran green.

Type surface:

- `tsc --noEmit -p packages/services/service-settings` → **13 errors, the ledgered count** in `scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs`, i.e. this change adds none. (One was introduced en route — `InMemoryCryptoProvider` is a value-only alias and cannot be spelled as a type — and fixed by using `LocalCryptoProvider` in the test.)
- Downstream consumer sweep, **prefix direction** (`--filter '...@objectstack/service-settings'` = the 9 packages that consume it, not its upstream deps): `turbo run typecheck` → **72 tasks successful, 72 total**. No reverse type-verification is reported because the change is purely **additive** to the public type surface (a new module, a new method) — nothing was narrowed, so there is no key a rebuilt `.d.ts` should now reject.
- `node scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs` → OK.

No `objectui` change is required: the mask is presence-preserving and the echoed-mask write is a no-op, so today's console keeps working unmodified.
